subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw treat enrolled-speaker verification as a native core voice security boundary, a provider/plugin capability, or defer it until the native STT abstraction is designed?
rationale: The request is valuable but changes command authorization, raw microphone handling, biometric-like state, and provider audio egress, so automation cannot infer the safe product/security contract from current code alone.

options.title: Design native speaker gate first
options.body: Create a maintainer-approved design for enrollment, local profile storage, thresholds, fallback, deletion, and which voice modes are gated before any implementation PR.

options.title: Fold into broader STT/provider work
options.body: Track speaker identification as a requirement of the custom ASR/native audio roadmap instead of adding a separate voiceprint surface now.

options.title: Defer speaker identity
options.body: Keep current wake-word, push-to-talk, and Talk behavior unchanged until security and biometric-state requirements are clearer.

recommendation.title: Design native speaker gate first
recommendation.body: Create a maintainer-approved design for enrollment, local profile storage, thresholds, fallback, deletion, and which voice modes are gated before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest provenance across the native macOS voice/Talk surfaces and the product/API boundary this decision would affect.
